newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Red River to see two inches of rain Monday.
newsitem.headline: Canada Red River to see two inches of rain Monday.

text.p: Canada's Red River Valley was forecast to see up to 50 mm (2.0 inches) Monday night after the Prairies saw light amounts of rain over the weekend.
"The Red River Valley and east to Ontario should see 35 to up to 50 mm of rain tonight and another five to 10 mm Tuesday," Environment Canada meteorologist Dale Marciski said.
Spring wheat began heading across the southern grainbelt late last week while crops further north were tillering or jointing, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Wheat's heading stage is when it needs water most.
Alberta saw little rain over the weekend with two mm recorded in the Peace River Valley Saturday and eight mm around Calgary Saturday and Sunday.

No rain fell anywhere in Saskatchewan on Saturday but Lucky Lake saw 23 mm (one inch) on Sunday, Maple Creek in the heart of the durum wheat growing area saw 20 mm while Regina and Yorkton each saw 16 mm.
Estevan, in the dry southeast of Saskatchewan, only saw three mm (0.12 inch) of rain on Sunday.
Manitoba saw no rain over the weekend.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat range from 30 to 32 bu/ac but CWB cut them June 11 to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac due to dryness.

A triangular area from Calgary to Lethbridge to Empress, Alberta, was rated very dry with the soil holding less than 30 percent of its optimum moisture capacity, Environment Canada soil scientist Rick Raddatz said.
All of southern Saskatchewan except for the southwestern districts around Maple Creek were rated dry with the soil holding less than 60 percent of optimum moisture capacity.
Southwest Manitoba was also rate dry, Raddatz added.
Soil moisture data was drawn from 160 Prairie stations on Monday June 23.
